about: Merum Priorati was founded in 2004 by two Catalan families, with backing from the Pere Ventura family, known for their Cava in the nearby Penedès. The estate lies outside Porrera, in the eastern part of the Priorat, sheltered by the Montsant range and cooled at night by air from the Mediterranean. Of more than 100 hectares across three parcels, only about a quarter is planted, on terraces so steep that vineyards here are counted in vines rather than hectares. The 2018 Destí was No. 4 in Wine Spectator’s Top 100 of 2021.

Destí, Catalan for “destiny,” is the estate’s flagship. The 2022 is 60 percent Garnacha, 30 percent Cariñena and 10 percent Syrah from 25-year-old vines on licorella, the broken black slate that defines Priorat. Grapes are hand-picked into small boxes, fermented in temperature-controlled steel with three weeks on the skins, then moved by gravity into 500-litre barrels, new and second-use, for malolactic fermentation and about 15 to 18 months of aging. It is bottled without fining or filtration and rests at least six months before release.

Critics found wild strawberry, plum, black raspberry and red licorice in the 2022, with cracked pepper, a velvety texture and a mineral finish; Decanter called it fresh and very approachable, with soft tannins. Wine Enthusiast called it full-bodied yet mouthwatering, with dried cranberry, cherry and Mediterranean spice over silken tannins, and suggested mountain stews, jamón and firm cheeses alongside. It is a modern, polished Priorat that still carries the region’s mineral signature.
facts: Steel fermentation; malolactic in 500 L barrels; unfined, unfiltered
